title: Forked programs nobody calls: PROGV2 / PROGOLD beside the live PROG
realism: Every real estate carries forks: a V2 rewrite that never went live, an OLD version kept for audit, or (TAXR) a V2 that replaced the original, which was never deleted. Their code looks live; only the estate's references say which one runs.
shapes: ORDVALV2 and ORDVOLD beside the live ORDVAL (ORDR)
TAXCALC replaced by TAXCALC2, which the job runs (TAXR)
SHPINQO, the pre-CICS-TS version of SHPINQ (SHIP)
asserts: A program no CALL, LINK, XCTL, EXEC PGM or TRANSACTION in the estate resolves to is dead: nothing draws an invocation edge to it. Its own code is still keyed in full.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Programming Guide (SC27-8714-03)
citations.quote: The program-name in the PROGRAM-ID paragraph or ENTRY statement must be identical to the corresponding program object name or program object alias of the program object that contains the program.

Use the PGM parameter to name the program that the system is to execute. The specified program must be a member of a partitioned data set (PDS) or partitioned data set extended (PDSE) used as a system library, a private library, or a temporary library.

dead.name: ORDVALV2
dead.why: a rewrite never put into production: no CALL, job step or CSD entry names ORDVALV2

dead.name: ORDVOLD
dead.why: replaced by ORDVAL in 1998: no CALL, job step or CSD entry names ORDVOLD

compile.reason: COPY SHPRATE: the estate holds no copybook SHPRATE (H-0053), so no compiler finds it
compile.check_note: EXEC blocks stubbed; a one-byte FILLER stands in for the missing COPY SHPRATE

dead.name: SHPINQO
dead.why: the pre-migration SHPINQ: no transaction, LINK or XCTL names SHPINQO

dead.name: TAXCALC
dead.why: replaced by TAXCALC2: no CALL or job step names TAXCALC
